title: Depth under localization is bounded by the quotient dimension
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], meaning that $R$ has exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $M$ be a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be a prime ideal and write $R_{\mathfrak p}=(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}R$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $M_{\mathfrak p}=(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}M$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. With depth taken at the maximal ideals of the respective local rings [def-weil-pbc-depth] and $\dim$ denoting ring Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], one has $$\operatorname{depth}_R(M)\leq\operatorname{depth}_{R_{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p})+\dim(R/\mathfrak p).$$ The zero module and zero localization are allowed, with depth $\infty$ and the usual extended-natural-number addition.

source.place: Tag 0FCC, lemma-depth-localization, statement at lines 18023–18026; depth of a finite module after localization.

proof.text: Put $S=R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $d=\dim(R/\mathfrak p)$. If $M_{\mathfrak p}=0$, its depth is $\infty$ by [def-weil-pbc-depth], so the inequality holds, including when $M=0$. Otherwise $M\ne0$. The prime-localization definition makes $S$ local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak pS$, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] makes it Noetherian. A finite generating set $m_1,\ldots,m_r$ for any finite $R$-module $N$ localizes to the generators $m_i/1$ of $N_{\mathfrak p}$: write $m/s=\sum_i(a_i/s)(m_i/1)$ when $m=\sum_i a_im_i$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-depth-ext], applied over $R$ and over $S$, says the depths of $N$ and $N_{\mathfrak p}$ are finite integers whenever these modules are nonzero. Finally $R/\mathfrak p$ is a nonzero domain, so its zero prime gives $d\ge0$; if $d=\infty$ the desired inequality is automatic. Henceforth assume $d<\infty$.

source.place: Tag 0FCC, lemma-depth-localization, first sentence; Tags 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 00LW (lemma-depth-ext), and 00LI (definition-depth) for the induction prerequisites.

proof.text: Fix $R$ and $\mathfrak p$. Use strong induction on the finite integer $n=\operatorname{depth}_R(N)$, uniformly for all nonzero finite $R$-modules $N$ with $N_{\mathfrak p}\ne0$. The claim is $n\le\operatorname{depth}_S(N_{\mathfrak p})+d$. If $n\le d$, nonnegativity of depth proves the claim; in particular this proves the base $n=0$. Assume $n>d$ and that the claim holds for every finite module of depth less than $n$ whose localization is nonzero.

source.place: Tag 0FCC, lemma-depth-localization, second sentence and final induction sentence; the induction is uniform in the module.

proof.text: No associated prime $\mathfrak q$ of $N$ contains $\mathfrak p$. Indeed, [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-dim-associated-prime] gives $n\le\dim(R/\mathfrak q)$. If $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$, the surjection $R/\mathfrak p\twoheadrightarrow R/\mathfrak q$ pulls every chain of prime ideals back to a chain of the same length: inverse images are prime by the product test, and strictness follows from surjectivity. Thus the chain definition of Krull dimension gives $\dim(R/\mathfrak q)\le d$, contradicting $n>d$.

source.place: Tag 0FCC, lemma-depth-localization, third sentence, invoking Tag 0BK4, lemma-depth-dim-associated-primes.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-associated-primes-finite], $\operatorname{Ass}_R(N)$ is finite. It is nonempty: $0$ is a zerodivisor on the nonzero module $N$, so [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-module-zerodivisors-union-associated-primes] puts $0$ in some associated prime. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] with $J=\mathfrak p$ and the finite nonempty list of associated primes. Step 3 verifies that $J$ is contained in none of them; all ideals in the list are prime. We obtain $x\in\mathfrak p$ outside their union. The same zerodivisor characterization says multiplication by $x$ on $N$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 0FCC, lemma-depth-localization, choice of x; Tags 00LC (lemma-finite-ass), 00DS (lemma-silly), and 00LD (lemma-ass-zero-divisors).

proof.text: Let $Q=N/xN$, a finite $R$-module generated by the images of any finite generating set of $N$. Localize the short exact sequence $0\to N\xrightarrow{x}N\to Q\to0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] the localized multiplication is injective and the map $N_{\mathfrak p}\to Q_{\mathfrak p}$ is surjective with kernel $xN_{\mathfrak p}$. Consequently $Q_{\mathfrak p}\cong N_{\mathfrak p}/xN_{\mathfrak p}$, by the $S$-linear map sending the class of $m/s$ to $(m\bmod xN)/s$; its kernel and surjectivity are exactly the preceding assertions. This also identifies their depths: an $S$-linear isomorphism carries each regular sequence and its successive quotients bijectively to the corresponding ones. The images of generators show $Q_{\mathfrak p}$ is finite over $S$, as in step 1.

source.place: Tag 0FCC, lemma-depth-localization, the localized quotient used in the penultimate sentence; Tag 00CS (proposition-localization-exact) and its immediate quotient consequence Tag 02C8 (lemma-localize-quotient-modules).
Tag 0FCC, lemma-depth-localization, simultaneous depth drop, invoking Tag 090R (lemma-depth-drops-by-one), part (1), first over R and then over R_p.

proof.text: Now $Q$ is finite with depth $n-1<n$ and has nonzero localization, so the induction hypothesis gives $n-1\le(t-1)+d$. All three quantities $n,t,d$ are finite nonnegative integers and $n,t\ge1$. Add $1$ to get $n\le t+d$. This proves the induction step and hence the claim for $N=M$. The cases removed in step 1 already prove the full extended-depth assertion.

source.place: Tag 0FCC, lemma-depth-localization, final sentence: induction on depth(M).

(5) Localization exactness gives x injective on N_p and Q_p isomorphic to N_p/xN_p; depth is invariant under isomorphism. (6) lem-depth-drops-by-one applies over R (x in p, inside m) and over S (x/1 in pS, injective, N_p nonzero finite, S Noetherian local); every hypothesis is checked.
